newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan says reform is a process, not one-off event.
newsitem.headline: Annan says reform is a process, not one-off event.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Thursday he needed more time to reform the United Nations than God took to create the universe because the Almighty did not have to deal with committees.
"I know that some feel that the reform process has not moved fast enough," the U.N. chief told a news conference six weeks after taking office pledging to reinvigorate the 185-member organisation.

He joked that at a recent lunch with Security Council members, "the Russian ambassador was quick to point out that I had had more time than God did" -- an allusion to the six days of creation mentioned in the Bible.
"But I also pointed out ... that He had a great advantage of working alone, without committees and without 185 members."

Stressing that reform was "a process, not an event," he said he would "take those measures which are within my authority in streamlining the secretariat and improving the managerial processes without waiting for government approval."
He also promised a report by the end of July outlining everything that had been done and submitting proposals for further reform that required the approval of U.N. member governments.

A two-page paper was circulated listing reform measures to date. These included the appointment of a special coordinator, the introduction of a Cabinet-style administration, steps to eliminate overlap and promote teamwork, and the scrapping of the posts of three senior advisers.
Annan has also ordered a 25 percent reduction in paperwork during 1997 by lowering the current page limit for Security Council documents from 24 to 16 and of General Assembly documents from 32 to 24.

"In sum, the secretary-general is committed to achieving a leaner, more efficient and more effective United Nations that is relevant to the challenges of the post-Cold War world, which is also the aim of member states," the paper said.
